section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch15 — History of Education: Commissions
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The Education Commission (1964–66), popularly known as the Kothari Commission, is famous for recommending which uniform school structure across India?
explanation: The Kothari Commission recommended the 10+2+3 structure, adopted through the National Policy on Education, 1968.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch15 — History of Education: Commissions
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The University Education Commission (1948-49), which recommended setting up the UGC, was chaired by:
explanation: The 1948-49 Commission, chaired by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, recommended establishing the UGC. Kothari chaired the later 1964-66 Education Commission.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: According to the National Curriculum Framework 2005, the teacher's ideal role in the classroom shifts from being a mere transmitter of information to being a:

options.option_text: Facilitator who helps learners construct their own knowledge
Strict disciplinarian focused only on control
Passive observer with no active role
Sole authority whose word cannot be questioned

explanation: NCF 2005 envisions constructivist, learner-centred pedagogy where the teacher facilitates active knowledge construction.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The RTE Act's Schedule prescribes a pupil-teacher ratio for primary classes (I–V) of:
explanation: The RTE norms specify a PTR of 30:1 at primary level (I–V) and 35:1 at upper-primary level (VI–VIII).

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The national mission launched in 2021 to implement NEP 2020's priority — that every child attains reading, writing and arithmetic by Grade 3 — is:
explanation: NIPUN Bharat (2021) operationalises the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Mission by Grade 3 — NEP 2020's declared 'highest priority'.
